hypotheses: A/L is a CM abelian surface
A admits an embedding of a quaternion division algebra over Q into End^0(A_bar)
Every geometric endomorphism of A is defined over L

sources.title: Nouveaux theoremes d'isogenie

sources.application: Source A'=(E')^2 over L, target A over L, g=2, base extension trivial. The general Xi^2 assertion is used, not the stronger MM assertion. Xi=(14^32*d*max(1,log d,h_F(A')))^8.

sources.authors: Adrian Barquero-Sanchez, Lindsay Cadwallader, Olivia Cannon, Tyler Genao and Riad Masri
sources.title: Faltings heights of CM elliptic curves and special Gamma values
sources.publication: Research in Number Theory 3, article 13 (2017), published 5 June 2017
locators: Section 1: original Faltings/Silverman normalization and definition of stable height
Section 6, equation (6.2): individual complex embedding discriminant formula
Section 7, proof of Theorem 1.3: CM potential good reduction and removal of the finite discriminant term after extension
sources.verification: Read full publisher HTML, including the Weierstrass-coefficient hypothesis in Proposition 6.1 and its distinction from the individual-embedding formula (6.2).
sources.application: Use equation (6.2) on a good-reduction extension to evaluate stable height. No class-average formula or coefficient descent to Q(j) is asserted. The subsequent eta-product estimate is proved in the local proof.
sources.underlying_classical_source: Joseph H. Silverman, Heights and elliptic curves, Arithmetic Geometry (1986), pp253-265, Proposition 1.1; cited explicitly by the published 2017 formula.

proved_steps: Quaternion division action excludes a geometrically simple CM surface, a product of nonisogenous elliptic curves, and the square of a non-CM elliptic curve.
Rational idempotents and all homomorphisms of elliptic factors descend to L because End(A_bar)=End_L(A).
The differential of CM endomorphisms embeds the quadratic field F into L.
For f O_F contained in End(E), the finite subgroup sum_i (f alpha_i)(E[f]) is defined over L and its quotient has analytic lattice O_F Lambda, hence maximal order. No extension of L is taken.
The discriminant tower formula and the shape of quadratic fundamental discriminants give abs(disc F)<=4 rad(abs(D_L)).
Reduced quadratic parameters and the eta product give h_F(E')<sqrt(abs(disc F))+1<=3R.
The isogeny-height inequality follows from pullback of determinant differentials: half log degree minus a nonnegative finite cokernel term.
Elementary logarithmic bounds give 854R, below the original 6^100 R^24 allowance.
not_used: Any joint von Kaenel-Kret theorem or unpublished CM height bound
Any assumption identifying CM with GR2023's separate MM property
Any field-degree bound on a semistable/good-reduction extension used only to evaluate stable height
A new witness, equation, coefficient, or constant in the original polynomial
not_certified_here: Existence of the field L with degree at most 576
Ramification support rad(D_L)<=R from the Shimura-curve model
The comparison of parameter height with stable Faltings height
The complete original H5 or the complete polynomial theorem
